meta.title: Context manager
meta.description: Session context management plugin: adds a Context manager entry (the list icon on the right of the session header) to the session header and manages the model context of a DSH session — delete messages one by one or whole turns, and restore them later. Two typical uses: roll back to the start of a turn and ask again (use /ctxmgr turns to read the turn numbers, then /ctxmgr deleteturn 5 to move that whole turn out of the context), and drop noise such as error logs, pasted code and trial-and-error instructions entry by entry (use /ctxmgr list to find the indexes, then /ctxmgr delete 12,13,14). The context_manager tool offers the same operations (actions list / list-turns / delete / delete-turns / restore). Deleting appends an empty developer message (a tombstone) that replaces the range on the session surface, so the raw session log, the chat transcript and audit data stay intact and removed messages disappear only from later model requests. Turns are listed with numbers, previews and an in-progress marker. Operations that cannot append safely are written into the session log as plugin records and applied at the next request, so they survive restarts; restore puts user and context messages back at their original position and appends assistant content at the tail. Local only, nothing leaves the machine. Requires a running session; system prompts and messages that are still streaming cannot be deleted. Turning the plugin off removes the header entry, the command and the tool, while tombstones already written stay in the log.
